title: Coefficient reductions are scalar cokernels
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, A its valuation ring and varpi the recorded uniformizer. Let X be any scheme. Use the continuous coefficient sheaves, scalar maps, normalized towers and quotient predicate of [def-per-integral-lisse-reduction-data]. For every n, the actual reduction from the integral coefficient unit to the restricted unit over A/(varpi^(n+1)) is a cokernel of multiplication by varpi^(n+1) in the category of sheaf A_X-modules.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1),(2), Definition 6.8.3, Proposition 6.8.4(1), p. 59; the reduction ring identification is the rank-one reduction in this proposition.

proof.text:
choose one integral representative of each finite residue value. Since the
quotient ring is discrete, composition with this finite section lifts every
continuous residue-valued function to a continuous integral-valued function.
The kernel consists of functions valued in the uniformizer-power ideal.
Multiplication by the nonzero uniformizer power identifies the integral ring
homeomorphically with this ideal: its inverse is division in the coefficient
field, with the subspace topology. Hence the kernel is precisely the image of
the scalar map, on every object and compatibly with restriction. The resulting
sectionwise cokernel is already the displayed finite-coefficient sheaf; therefore
it has the sheaf cokernel universal property as well.

theorem integralLisseCoefficient_quotients (n : ℕ) :
    IsIntegralLisseQuotient l E X
      (Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E ^ (n + 1))
      (integralLisseRingMap l E X
        ((sheafCompose _ (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).map
          (integralLisseReduction l E X n)))
